messages:
mike_cheng: alerting — seeing a sharp p99 spike on inference.gateway starting ~14:03 UTC, p99 ~2.7s, streaming stalls increasing. paging @sre_oncall @kevin @anya. looks correlated with configfetch errors and token-store 500s.

incident-bot: SLO ALERT — inference.gateway p99 exceeded (threshold 1.5s). 5m window: p99=2.73s, error ratio 4.8%, streaming stall rate +120%.

sre_oncall: oncall here, grabbing dashboards. which customers impacted and any mitigation already attempted?

mike_cheng: quick summary: a feature-flag rollout increased configfetch fanout; config-store started timing out on auth calls. gateway shows many `auth_fetch failed 503` with retries. also seeing DB token-store elevated 5xx.

anya: digging logs — configstore latency climbed from 60ms -> 800ms in last 6m. auth-db (token-store) p95 ~1.2s, p99 ~2.4s. stacktrace from gateway shows queueing at controlplane before inference proxy.

kevin: can we toggle the FF? if the flag causes extra per-request fetches we should rollback to stop the fanout. who has access to the console?

eli: customer-impact: two mid-market customers reported streaming stalls and partial responses for embeddings. CS alerted; raising to medium severity for now.

ops-bot: ```
$ curl -sS https://token-store.internal/healthz
{"status":"degraded","db_connections": 450, "errors_last_min": 72}
logs: token_fetcher: timeout->503; retry=3; pool_wait=120ms
```

sre_oncall: thanks. DB connections look high. can infra throttle incoming configfetch QPS at the gateway as a short-term mitigation? also will check for cache hit ratios.

mike_cheng: started a lightweight routing change: gateway will route non-critical configfetches to cached-catalog (local fallback) while we roll back ff. deploying canary now.

incident-bot: DEPLOY EVENT — canary rollout 10% for gateway fallback routing. monitor at /dashboards/inference/gateway/latency.

kevin: executing rollback: `redwoodctl feature rollback ff/new-config-fanout --env=prod` (console shows in progress).

anya: suggestion: increase TTL for feature-flag lookups and add a short in-process cache on gateway to avoid round trips per request. that will reduce controlplane QPS by ~60% in perf tests.

sre_oncall: applying connection-limiter on gateway for configfetch endpoints (200rps/instance) to smooth bursts. watching metrics.

mike_cheng: limiter applied. p99 dropped to ~1.4s within 3m, error ratio down to 1.9%, streaming stalls reduced noticeably. rolling limiter to all instances.

customer-success: sent status update: "We're experiencing a degraded service for a subset of streaming requests. We've applied throttles and reverted a recent flag rollout; our engineers are continuing mitigations. More updates in 30m." :message: :loud_sound:

eli: tagging for follow-up: need post-incident eval for token-store retries, configfetch circuit breaker, and safer default behavior if flags fail. also add customer RCA draft.

sre_oncall: will remain on this until handoff. plan: 1) confirm canary rollback success 2) observe for 30m 3) handoff to @oncall-next with notes.

oncall-next: I'll take 30–60m after lunch. please leave runbook notes in thread.

mike_cheng: follow-ups captured: increase flag TTLs, add circuit breaker on configfetch, implement short in-process LRU cache, reduce token-store retry storm by exponential backoff cap, and add GA rollback guard for flag fanout changes.

incident-bot: Incident logged. Create ticket: ENG-INC-2648 (postmortem required if >2hr impact). timeline appended to ticket.

sre_oncall: leaving notes for handoff: limiter applied; FF rollback in progress; canary metrics trending down; watch `inference.gateway.streaming_stall_rate` and `token_store.errors_last_min`. escalate to infra-team if DB connections > 500.

kevin: confirmed rollback finished. console shows flag state restored to previous.

mike_cheng: thanks. we'll draft customer communication and plan follow-up review.

eli: setting priority P2 and scheduling postmortem meeting for tomorrow morning.

incident-bot: action items: ["rollback verified","throttle applied","create postmortem","CS updates sent"].

sre_oncall: handing off to @oncall-next in 30m. leaving channel open for any quick escalations.

oncall-next: ack — will monitor and pick up.

mike_cheng: closing loop for now. good job team. :thumbsup:
